skill.name: scanpy
skill.description: Guide Scanpy single-cell RNA-seq analysis from data loading through quality control, normalization, clustering, marker discovery, annotation, and visualization.
skill.summary: Run structured single-cell RNA-seq analysis workflows with Scanpy guidance, templates, and QC scripts.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Single-cell RNA-seq workflows can be hard to organize across QC, clustering, annotation, and plots. This skill provides Scanpy guidance, scripts, and references for reproducible analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains loading .h5ad, 10X, and CSV matrices into AnnData.
Guides quality control metrics, filtering thresholds, and plot review.
Covers normalization, PCA, UMAP, t-SNE, and Leiden clustering workflows.
Shows marker gene discovery and manual cell type annotation patterns.
Includes a QC script and full analysis template for local Python execution.
Provides plotting and API references for publication-focused figures.
limitations: Requires a local Python environment with Scanpy and related packages installed.
Does not validate biological conclusions or replace expert review.
Example thresholds must be tuned for each dataset and tissue type.
Large datasets may need more memory, batch correction, or specialized tooling.

use_cases.title: Run first-pass quality control
use_cases.description: Use the QC script and guidance to inspect cells, genes, and mitochondrial percentages before deeper analysis.

use_cases.title: Build a reproducible analysis workflow
use_cases.description: Adapt the template to load data, normalize counts, reduce dimensions, cluster cells, and save intermediate outputs.

use_cases.title: Prepare publication figures
use_cases.description: Use the plotting guide to create UMAP, marker, trajectory, and multi-panel visualizations with consistent settings.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Scanpy analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me start a Scanpy analysis for my single-cell RNA-seq dataset. Ask for the input format and suggest the first QC steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose QC thresholds
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my dataset summary and recommend Scanpy QC thresholds for genes per cell, counts, and mitochondrial percentage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan clustering and annotation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Scanpy plan for normalization, highly variable genes, PCA, neighbors, UMAP, Leiden clustering, and marker-based annotation.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an advanced workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my Scanpy workflow for batch effects, clustering resolution, marker validation, trajectory analysis, and reproducible output checkpoints.

output_examples.input: I have a 10X dataset and need a first analysis plan.
output_examples.output: A staged Scanpy workflow covering data loading, QC review, filtering, normalization, dimensionality reduction, clustering, markers, and saved outputs.

output_examples.input: My UMAP clusters need cell type labels.
output_examples.output: A marker-based annotation approach that compares known genes across clusters and records assumptions for biological review.

output_examples.input: I need plots for a manuscript figure.
output_examples.output: A figure plan with UMAP, dot plot, heatmap, and QC panels using consistent labels, palettes, and export settings.

best_practices: Save raw counts and intermediate AnnData checkpoints before major transformations.
Tune QC thresholds from plots and dataset context instead of fixed defaults.
Validate cluster annotations with multiple marker genes and documented assumptions.
anti_patterns: Using default QC thresholds without checking dataset-specific distributions.
Assigning cell types from one marker gene without supporting evidence.
Skipping batch effect review when samples, donors, or runs differ.

faq.question: What data formats does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers .h5ad, 10X Genomics matrices, 10X HDF5 files, and CSV expression matrices.

faq.question: Does the skill run Scanpy by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, references, a QC script, and a template that users run in their local environment.

faq.question: Can it annotate cell types automatically?
faq.answer: It supports manual marker-based annotation patterns, but biological validation remains the user responsibility.

faq.question: Does it include plotting guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for QC plots, UMAP, marker plots, trajectory plots, and publication-focused settings.

faq.question: Can it help with batch correction?
faq.answer: Yes. It mentions Scanpy ComBat and points to separate methods such as Harmony or scVI when needed.

faq.question: Is it suitable for large datasets?
faq.answer: It can guide large analyses, but memory use and performance depend on the local Python environment and dataset size.
